title: The Price of Knowledge
summary: Nasruddin spent years offering free advice on farming, health, and peace in the village square, but nobody listened to him....
full_text:
Nasruddin spent years offering free advice on farming, health, and peace in the village square, but nobody listened to him.

One day, he put on a grand embroidered robe, hung a brass sign reading "Supreme Master of Secrets," and charged ten gold dinars for a single question.

A wealthy landlord paid the ten gold coins and asked: "Tell me, Master: what is the most profound secret of human life?"

Nasruddin pocketed the gold and whispered: "The greatest secret is this: never give ten gold dinars to a man who sells words!"
moral: True knowledge is priceless, but people only value what costs them dear.
